description: ALLOCATE statement (dynamic storage), ISO §2023:14.9.3 - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ALLOCATE is no ANSI X3.23-1985 statement and no 1985 reserved word, since §2002:F.1 item 6 ("The following reserved words have been added") lists ALLOCATE; §2002:14.8.3 adds "The ALLOCATE statement obtains dynamic storage" (§2002:14.8.3.2 SR1: "The data item referenced by data-name-1 shall be described with the BASED clause"), and §2002:F.2 item 47 states the change: "ALLOCATE and FREE statements are provided for obtaining storage dynamically." §2014:14.9.3 and §2023:14.9.3.1 carry the 2002 sentence unchanged. ACTIVE: both formats bind (n CHARACTERS RETURNING p -> a fresh StorageCell window pointer, GR1 round-up / GR2 <=0 -> NULL no EC / GR6 INITIALIZED zero-fill; based-item -> the implicit pointer takes a cell of the template width, GR3/GR4a/GR4b) and the based INITIALIZED form lowers per GR7 to the spec's INITIALIZE ... WITH FILLER ALL TO VALUE THEN TO DEFAULT expansion (a BoundSequence over the ONE INITIALIZE mechanism; golden 2002/allocate_initialized). INITIALIZED is a phrase of this gated statement - no separate matrix row (the phrase-level precedent).
